alternate_names: Thakur Ji Shree Raj Ranchhodji Temple

history.summary: Red sandstone Krishna temple built in 1905 by Queen Jadechi Rajkanwar after the death of her husband Maharaja Jaswant Singh of Marwar. She installed the black marble idol of Ranchhodji (Krishna) that she had brought with her at her marriage from Gujarat, along with priests from Gujarat whose descendants still serve the temple. The temple features fine carvings and filigree work, and stained-glass windows (green, yellow, blue) on the main entrance door. It stands raised on ~50 steps, giving views over the railway station area. FLAG: one review aggregator (Wanderlog) calls it a 17th-century temple - this conflicts with all other sources citing 1905; treated as an error. FLAG: town is Jodhpur (Banar Road / Baiji Ka Talab, Ratanada area, near MG Hospital Road and Sojati Gate); CSV town 'Jodhpur' is correct.

name: Raj Ranchhodji Temple
town_description: Jodhpur, the 'Blue City' and 'Sun City' of Rajasthan, is the historic capital of Marwar founded by Rao Jodha in 1459. Dominated by the massive Mehrangarh Fort, it is Rajasthan's second-largest city and a major tourist hub for Rajput heritage, blue-painted old-town houses, textiles, and handicrafts.

travel.railway: Walkable/short ride from Jodhpur Junction (Banar Road / MG Hospital Road side)
travel.road: ~3.5 km from central Jodhpur; reachable by bus, taxi, or auto-rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami for decorations; sunset for city views from the raised platform
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:30 AM to 12:00 PM and 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM
